bugs.name: Remote Browser test error toast clipped beyond right viewport
bugs.summary: A long Remote Browser connection-test error is reported as clipped or defective when its diagnostic lines and separators wrap inside the toast.
bugs.expected: Connection diagnostics should be readable within the viewport.
bugs.actual: The report claimed clipped diagnostic text. The human-reviewed screenshot shows the complete error text and separators wrapping visibly inside the toast.
reproSteps: As an authenticated administrator, open Settings > Remote Browsers > Add Remote Browser.
Enter a fresh friendly name and ws://127.0.0.1:1 without saving the browser.
Click Test and inspect the connection-refused toast after its entrance animation.
Observe that long diagnostic lines and separators wrap within the readable toast.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected L14: the screenshot shows readable wrapped text, not clipping. Normal wrapping of the connection diagnostics and long separator is not a bug. This reference does not reject a different report that demonstrates genuinely clipped or missing text.

bugs.name: Remote Browser test error toast disappears after five seconds
bugs.summary: The Remote Browser connection-test error toast automatically disappears after about five seconds without leaving a persistent error on the form.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the connection-test error should remain visible rather than automatically disappear after five seconds.
bugs.actual: The error toast disappears after about five seconds while the Add Remote Browser form remains open.
reproSteps: As an authenticated administrator, open Settings > Remote Browsers > Add Remote Browser.
Enter a fresh friendly name and ws://127.0.0.1:1 without saving the browser.
Click Test and observe the expected connection-refused error toast.
Wait about five seconds and observe that the toast dismisses while the form remains open.
bugs.reason: Human review rejected the five-second disappearance claim in L14. Remote Browser Test uses the normal toast error path without a timeout override, and the pinned vue-toastification dependency defaults to 5000ms. Automatic dismissal after about five seconds is expected behavior, not a bug; no persistent form-error result is promised.
